llm.summary: The patent-comparison workflow is coherent, but its handling of paid API keys needs review because credentials can reach an unintended server.

dimensions.detail: patentmax_client.py:65,324–344 attaches credentials to an environment-configurable server without enforcing HTTPS or an approved origin. An offline check confirmed that its default redirect handler retains Authorization across hosts and HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled Python client uses standard-library modules. No dependency installation, remote code execution, or installation hooks were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main workflow limits comparisons to two or three patents and discloses costs. Broader search instructions include confidentiality checks and user checkpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: patentmax_client.py:69–88 automatically reuses ~/.patentmax/api_key.txt and instructs the agent to request a paid key through chat and save it there. Unlike the trial-key file, this paid-key workflow specifies no restrictive file permissions or destination binding. No background services or scheduled persistence were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to retrieve claims, compare technical features, and write a CSV. The broader client is explicitly documented as shared patent tooling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Prefer the free trial until credential handling is fixed. Avoid pasting paid keys into chat, restrict access to saved keys, and require protection against sending credentials to another server. Search terms go to PatentMax; approve confidential disclosures and agree on spending limits.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: The trial-registration claim is unsupported: that request sends a fixed source identifier, not credentials. Normal bearer authentication is expected, but unvalidated destinations and credential-preserving redirects substantiate a conditional key-exposure risk; actual exfiltration was not demonstrated.
[TP4] expected: The mismatch claims are overridden by the complete artifacts: comparison and CSV creation are agent instructions, while tools.md explicitly identifies the broader shared client. The FAQ prints eight-character key-type prefixes, which are documented constants rather than secret suffixes.
[LP1] expected: Environment-based authentication and API networking support the disclosed integration. The tool declaration alone does not establish a violated runtime permission boundary.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese conclusions fit this Chinese-language skill. This is a language preference, not a material security concern.
[E1] expected: The listed ip930.com destinations are the disclosed patent provider, console, and documentation links. Their presence does not establish unrelated data collection or exfiltration.
[SQP-2] expected: The package-level omission claim is downgraded: tools.md:144 explicitly requires checking for confidential invention details and states that technical information goes to the server. The main comparison workflow does not upload pasted claim text through the client.
[TT2] expected: Trial-key and candidate-ledger writes use the configurable PatentMax cache directory and support the disclosed workflow. These writes alone do not show unauthorized mutation; paid-key storage protections remain a separate concern.
